svg.text: Audi seat controller - OPTIMISED design (prototype, not built yet)
Current build + D1 (easier wake) + C1 (wake capacitor) + 0.96in I2C OLED. Build from enclosure-wiring.png until this has been tested.
Hammond 1599HBK | J1 seat side: switch panel + pushbutton (9-pin) | J2 power side: 12V in + 2 motor outputs (9-pin) | not to scale

g.text: Button wakes the module via DC+;
IN is jumpered to DC+ (mode P-3).
D1 stops the button feeding the Cytron,
buck and Nano - it only has to wake this.
linked to J1-7 on the block

svg.text: Inside the box wires are coloured by job. Outside J1 they are the pushbutton's real wire colours. Thin wires are 22 AWG; the KF2510 cable is 26 AWG. Not to scale.
Wiring list - CHANGED and NEW rows highlighted
Switch panel to Nano (22 AWG, 5V logic only)
parked - front tilt, no driver yet
parked - rear tilt, no driver yet
Pushbutton (22 AWG, 12V only - never to a Nano pin)
J1-7 short link on the block
LED fed from the NO line
feed is fused at F1 before J2
CHANGED: D1 1N5819 in line, stripe to DC+
OLED display (22 AWG, short - under about 30 cm)
Pushbutton rear view - 5-wire plug (colours read from your photos)
yellow NC -> not used - insulate the end
Not from a datasheet - confirm with a meter (checklist step 1) before relying on it.
Notes - numbered markers on the diagram
The button does not signal the Nano. Pressing it puts +12V on the module's own DC+ supply; IN is jumpered to DC+ (the maker lists IN as a
positive, high-level trigger). In mode P-3 the relay closes at once, stays on for the set time, then opens and stays off. Bench-tested (README).
F1 sits in the +12V feed before J2-5, as close to the supply as possible, rated from the motors' measured stall current and no more than 16 AWG
wire can carry - not yet decided (WIRING.md test T1). F2 is 1A on the buck converter's red input lead.
The Cytron MDD10A has no reverse-polarity protection: B+ must get the switched +12V from YYLOCK NO, B- must go to ground. D1 and C1 are
polarised too: D1 stripe towards DC+, C1 + leg to DC+. Fitted backwards, D1 stops the latch holding; C1 can fail and vent.
R1/R2 (10k) hold PWM1/PWM2 low while the Nano boots; PWM low = motor stopped whatever DIR is (Cytron manual). The firmware must
set up the motor pins before it starts the display, so a slow or missing OLED can never delay that.
J1-1 to J1-5: switch panel, 5V logic, to the Nano. J1-6 to J1-9: pushbutton, 12V, to the YYLOCK/J2 only. J1 is identical to the current
build, so the same harness plugs in. Only the wire behind J1-4 moves inside the box (A5 to A0).
WAGO A (power, 5 ports): Cytron B-, Nano GND, buck input -, J2-6 GND in, YYLOCK DC-. WAGO B (logic, 4 of 5 ports): switch PIN 4,
buck output -, OLED GND, and the link to the Nano's analog-row GND. Both meet through the Nano's two GND pins, which are joined on the board.
Without D1, the self-latch wire lets the button also feed NO - the Cytron, buck and Nano - until the relay closes. D1 (1N5819) blocks that, so a
press only has to wake the YYLOCK. C1 then holds DC+ up for a moment if the contact is short or bouncy. Untested: confirm with test T3.
I2C is fixed to A4 (SDA) / A5 (SCL), so recline moves to A0 (A6/A7 can't use INPUT_PULLUP). Needs new firmware: use a light library
(SSD1306Ascii or U8g2 page mode - 2KB RAM). Shown from the back as mounted in the lid, so its pin order is reversed: SDA, SCL, VCC, GND.
Wires per screw terminal (count them when you check)
YYLOCK DC+: 3 (button NO, D1 wire, IN jumper) + C1 soldered underneath | YYLOCK NO: 3 (Cytron B+, D1 wire, F2/buck) | IN: 1
YYLOCK DC-: 2 (WAGO A, LED-) + C1 underneath | Nano 5V: 2 (buck Y, OLED VCC) | Nano GND analog row: 1 (WAGO B) | Nano GND digital row: 2
J1-7: 2 (button NO, link) | J2-5 inside: 2 (COM, button C) | WAGO A: 5 of 5 | WAGO B: 4 of 5 (1 spare) | A4, A5, A0: 1 each
1 Button: with the plug on, meter blue-green beeps only while pressed; blue-yellow beeps when released. Diode test red/black to find LED +.
2 D1: meter diode test from NO to DC+ reads about 0.2-0.4V; reversed it reads open. C1: + leg on DC+, striped (-) side on DC-.
3 Check every row of the wiring list by continuity, terminal to terminal. Tug-test every screw terminal and WAGO lever.
4 No supply connected: J2-5 to J2-6 must NOT read near 0 ohms. Cytron B+ to B- must not read near 0 ohms.
5 Fit F1 (rating decided from stall current) and F2 (1A). Confirm the vehicle feed polarity at the J2 plug before connecting it.
6 First power-up with motor plugs J2-1..4 disconnected: a short, light press should now wake it every time. Nano 5V pin reads 4.75-5.25V.
7 Still without motors: M1A-M1B and M2A-M2B read 0V at rest, about 12V only while a seat switch is held. OLED shows text (new firmware).
8 Connect the motors and test each direction; confirm the 8 s run cutoff and that the YYLOCK switches everything off after its set time.
What changes from the current build
Parts to add: D1 1N5819, C1 330uF 25V (105C rated preferred), 0.96in I2C OLED, one more WAGO 221-415 (WAGO B), 22 AWG wire.
Wires that move: J1-4 recline A5 -> A0 (inside the box only), switch PIN 4 and buck B out from the Nano GND to WAGO B.
Wires added: WAGO B -> Nano GND, OLED SDA/SCL/VCC/GND. The self-latch wire gets D1 in line; C1 goes under the blue DC block.
Firmware: recline pin A5 -> A0, plus display code. The enclosure plugs (J1, J2) and everything on the 12V side stay exactly as built.
